key_insight: Local AI agents bring power-electronics simulation workflows on premises, making their capability and per-task power, energy, token and time costs important engineering considerations.
engineering_relevance: On-premises deployment supports workflows where sensitive designs must remain on site and simulators are locally licensed, but adds demand to local computing infrastructure.
method: Apply locally served models to agentic simulation tasks from converter to system level.
Measure power, energy, token use and elapsed time under comparable conditions.
Characterize capability boundaries and cost per solved task.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a systematic measurement framework but reports no numerical results, model comparisons or task success rates.
watch_item: Practical performance and cost advantages remain unquantified in the abstract and require validation on the intended hardware and simulation workload.
paper_title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
